- current state as JSON or a screenshot
- legal actions
- one-step action execution

I’m using the repo’s provenance-aware exploration guidance so the integration follows the project’s established architecture.

content.text:
Done, bud. JSHack now has a JSONL game-playing bridge.

Run:

```bash
deno task agent:play --seed 12648430 --class outlaw
```

It provides serialized map/entity/player state, inventory, spells, suggested actions, and accepts one action per input line.

Implemented:

- [agentView.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/main/runtime/agentView.js)
- [agent-player.mjs](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/tools/agent-player.mjs)
- [AGENT_PLAY.md](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/tools/AGENT_PLAY.md)
- Runtime integration and focused test

All architecture, event, tooling, and focused tests pass. I also drove turns through the bridge successfully. Say “play” and I’ll take the next dungeon turns myself.

I can play the headless rules version of JSHack, turn by turn.

I can:

- inspect the explored dungeon grid
- see visible monsters, items, doors, stairs, and interactables
- track HP, mana, stamina, hunger, effects, inventory, equipment, and spells
- move, attack, wait, search, loot, equip, drink/use/throw items, cast, shoot, interact, disarm traps, and traverse

I cannot currently see or click the rendered canvas like a human. I’m playing through the game’s actual rules engine, with the JSONL bridge translating each decision into a real game action.
do you start in a dungeon? hopefully yes because getting out of a town and into a dungeon would be tough -- to say the least.

Yes. The agent bridge defaults to `startDepth: 1`, so I begin inside a generated dungeon—not in town.

I start near the upward staircase, then explore the floor for monsters, loot, doors, and the downward staircase. Town/overworld only happens if we explicitly launch with `--depth 0`.
